text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The supervisory board of troubled heavy engineering and arms producer Povazske Strojarne last week dismissed its entire board of directors and replaced it with undisclosed people from the company's majority shareholders.

- The International Organisation of Tax Administration (IOTA), including tax administration bodies from 15 central and eastern Europe countries, will hold its first annual summit next September in Bratislava.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The British Know-How Fund will extend some 1.75 million stg over the next three years to support small and medium-sized enterprises, tourism and enviromental projects in the region around the central Slovak town of Ziar Nad Hronom.
- Natural gas is expected to account for about 35 percent of Slovakia's energy consumption by the year 2010.
- Oil and gas storage company Nafta Gbely said it would increase its storage capacity to 2.485 billion cubic metres of gas by the year 2002, from the current capacity of 1.7 billion cubic metres.
- The private military equipment maker Ales said it was considering creating a joint-venture with France's Thomson to produce military radars.
SME - The transport ministry has rejected media information that it was planning an increase in prices of the state-run bus and railway transport services from the beginning of next year.

PRAVDA - The opposition Party of Democratic Left (SDL) said it would support a move to take the case of the withdrawal of the parliamentary mandate of a former deputy for the ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS) to the Constitutional Court.
